rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zafīr is exhaling and shahīq is drawing breath back in; the terms are also used for the first and last parts of a donkey’s bray.
rows.anchor: الزفير إخراج النفس والشهيق رده، واستعمالها في أول النهيق وآخره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two sounds convey the damned’s severe anguish, likened either to heat constricting the heart and breath or to donkeys braying.
rows.anchor: الدلالة على شدة كربهم وغمهم وتشبيه حالهم بمن استولت الحرارة على قلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has shaqū with ḍamma on the initial consonant.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { شقوا } بالضم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase does not tie punishment’s duration to the heavens and earth: other texts establish Hell’s endless duration while those realms end; this is an Arab figure for eternity.
rows.anchor: ليس لارتباط دوامهم في النار بدوامهما فإن النصوص دالة على تأبيد دوامهم وانقطاع دوامهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even a literal linkage would not make punishment end when the heavens and earth end, or make their duration equal; their persistence is only an implied concomitant, and implication cannot outweigh explicit wording.
rows.anchor: لأن دوامهما كالملزوم لدوامه، وقد عرفت أن المفهوم لا يقاوم المنطوق

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative takes the heavens and earth to mean those of the afterlife, supported by the earth’s transformation in 14:48; the author objects that this analogy invokes an unknown duration and adds nothing for those who already know it lasts.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد سموات الآخرة وأرضها ويدل عليه قوله تعالى: يوم تبدل الأرض غير الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception covers sinful monotheists: they leave Hell, and are apart from Paradise during their punishment; their faith makes them blessed in one respect despite disobedience.
rows.anchor: بعضهم وهم فساق الموحدين يخرجون منها، وذلك كاف في صحة الاستثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The division remains valid because everyone at the gathering falls under the two states, even though one person can be wretched and blessed in different respects; strict mutual exclusion applies only to a truly disjoint division.
rows.anchor: وها هنا المراد أن أهل الموقف لا يخرجون عن القسمين، وأن حالهم لا يخلو عن السعادة والشقاوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other proposed exceptions are occasional transfers from Hell to the intensely cold region or other torments, and Paradise dwellers’ receiving delights beyond Paradise, such as divine nearness, favor, and vision.
rows.anchor: أو لأن أهل النار ينقلون منها إلى الزمهرير وغيره من العذاب أحيانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception may instead concern the initial period awaiting judgment, since the wording seems to place them in the Fire when the Day arrives, or their earthly and intermediate lives if the ruling is not day-limited.
rows.anchor: أو من أصل الحكم والمستثنى زمان توقفهم في الموقف للحساب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view makes the exception apply to the preceding statement that they have sighing and gasping in the Fire.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو من قوله: { لهم فيها زفير وشهيق }

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes illā as “besides”: God may add an endless duration beyond the time represented by the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: وقيل إلا ها هنا بمعنى سوى كقولك على ألف إلا الألفان القديمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God acts as He wills, without anyone being able to object.
rows.anchor: { إن ربك فعال لما يريد } من غير اعتراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Unsevered gift” explicitly states that reward does not end and shows that the exception in the reward passage does not mean cessation; reward and punishment are thus distinguished by their everlastingness.
rows.anchor: وهو تصريح بأن الثواب لا ينقطع وتنبيه على أن المراد من الاستثناء في الثواب ليس الانقطاع

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص
rows.claim: These readers vocalize saʿidū as passive, from saʿadahu Allāh, “God made him happy.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص { سعدوا } على البناء للمفعول من سعده الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾan is accusative either as an emphatic verbal noun (“they were given a gift”) or as a circumstantial accusative describing Paradise.
rows.anchor: و { عطاء } نصب على المصدر المؤكد أي أعطوا عطاء أو الحال من الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told not to doubt, after revelation, the people’s eventual fate.
rows.anchor: { فلا تك فى مرية } شك بعد ما أنزل عليك من مآل أمر الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The doubt concerns either the error of these polytheists’ worship, which leads to the fate of earlier idolaters, or the nature of their objects of worship, which can neither harm nor benefit.
rows.anchor: من عبادة هؤلاء المشركين في أنها ضلال مؤد إلى مثل ما حل بمن قبلهم

words: مَا يَعْبُدُونَ إِلَّا كَمَا يَعْبُدُ ءَابَآؤُهُم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement explains the warning: they share their ancestors’ polytheism, either worshipping as they did or worshipping the same kinds of idols, and will meet the same outcome because like causes yield like results.
rows.anchor: أي هم وآباؤهم سواء في الشرك، أي ما يعبدون عبادة إلا كعبادة آبائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past sense of kāna is understood in the comparison: “as their ancestors used to worship.”
rows.anchor: ومعنى { كما يعبد } كما كان يعبد فحذف للدلالة من قبل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their allotted share is either their full punishment like their ancestors’ or their provision, which explains why punishment is delayed despite its cause being present.
rows.anchor: { وإنا لموفوهم نصيبهم } حظهم من العذاب كآبائهم، أو من الرزق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Undiminished” is a circumstantial qualifier of the allotted share and limits “fulfilment,” since “fulfilment” can idiomatically describe giving only part.
rows.anchor: { غير منقوص } حال من النصيب لتقييد التوفية فإنك تقول: وفيته حقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unseen is what the senses cannot perceive; the manifest is what they can perceive.
rows.anchor: { علم الغيب } الغائب عن الحس. { والشهدة } الحاضر له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Kabīr means immense in rank, such that nothing lies outside His knowledge.
rows.anchor: { الكبير } العظيم الشأن الذي لا يخرج عن علمه شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Mutaʿāl means either exalted over everything through His power or beyond the descriptions of created beings.
rows.anchor: { المتعال } المستعلي على كل شيء بقدرته، أو الذي كبر عن نعت المخلوقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who keeps speech secret does so within himself; the one who speaks openly addresses another.
rows.anchor: { سواء منكم من أسر القول } في نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The night-time person is seeking concealment and hiding at night; the daytime sāِrib is exposed and visible to everyone, from saraba meaning to emerge.
rows.anchor: { ومن هو مستخف بالليل } طالب للخفاء في مختبأ بالليل. { وسارب } بارز

words: وَمَنْ هُوَ مُسْتَخْفٍۭ بِٱلَّيْلِ وَسَارِبٌۢ بِٱلنَّهَارِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sārib is coordinated either with man or with mustakhfin, construing man to include two people; the cited line uses man with a dual verb and illustrates this construction.
rows.anchor: وهو عطف على من أو مستخف على أن من في معنى الإثنين كقوله: نكن مثل من يا ذئب يصطحبان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse connects to the preceding one by affirming the perfection and comprehensiveness of God’s knowledge.
rows.anchor: والآية متصلة بما قبلها مقررة لكمال علمه وشموله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra contains fifty-two verses.
rows.anchor: وهي آياتها اثنتان وخمسون آية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kitāb is explained by an omitted demonstrative: “This is a Book.”
rows.anchor: { الر كتاب } أي هو كتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book was sent to the Prophet so that, by calling people to its contents, he would bring them out of error into guidance.
rows.anchor: { أنزلنه إليك لتخرج الناس } بدعائك إياهم إلى ما تضمنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Darknesses are the various kinds of misguidance, and light is guidance.
rows.anchor: { من الظلمت } من أنواع الضلال. { إلى النور } إلى الهدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By their Lord’s permission means through His enabling and facilitation, metaphorically borrowed from permission as the easing of a barrier.
rows.anchor: بتوفيقه وتسهيله مستعار من الاذن الذي هو تسهيل الحجاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “by their Lord’s permission” is attached to “bring out,” or construed circumstantially with its subject or object.
rows.anchor: وهو صلة { لتخرج } أو حال من فاعله أو مفعوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The path phrase either substitutes for “to the light,” repeating the preposition, or begins a new answer to an implied question about the destination.
rows.anchor: { إلى صراط العزيز الحميد } بدل من قوله: { إلى النور } بتكرير العامل أو استئناف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The path is attributed to God either because He is its destination or because He manifests it; the two attributes assure travelers that they will not be humbled or disappointed.
rows.anchor: إضافة الصراط إلى الله تعالى إما لأنه مقصده أو المظهر له وتخصيص الوصفين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham attributes misguidance to idols as its cause, as worldly life is said to have deceived people in 6:70, and therefore asks for protection from their misleading effect.
rows.anchor: وإسناد الإضلال إليهن باعتبار السببية كقوله تعالى وغرتهم الحيوة الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following Abraham means following his religion.
rows.anchor: فمن تبعنى على ديني فإنه منى أي بعضي لا ينفك في أمر الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The follower is “of me,” that is, like a part of Abraham and inseparable from him in religion.
rows.anchor: فإنه منى أي بعضي لا ينفك في أمر الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can forgive and show mercy to the disobedient either from the outset or after enabling repentance; every sin, even idolatry, is within His power to forgive, though the threat distinguishes it from other sins.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على أن كل ذنب فلله أن يغفره حتى الشرك إلا أن الوعيد فرق بينه وبين غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means some of my descendants or some descendants of my descendants; the omitted object is Ishmael and his offspring, whose settlement is implied by settling Ishmael.
rows.anchor: أي بعض ذريتي أو ذرية من ذريتي فحذف المفعول وهم إسماعيل ومن ولد منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The barren valley is Mecca, a rocky valley where plants do not grow.
rows.anchor: يعني وادي مكة فإنها حجرية لا تنبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Sacred House is called muḥarram because violating or neglecting it is forbidden, or because it has always been honored and feared by tyrants, or because the flood was kept from it, making it ʿatīq, “freed.”
rows.anchor: الذي حرمت التعرض له والتهاون به، أو لم يزل معظما ممنعا يهابه الجبابرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Abraham made this prayer on first arriving, he may have described the House according to its prior state or what it would later become.
rows.anchor: ولو دعا بهذا الدعاء أول ما قدم فلعله قال ذلك باعتبار ما كان أو ما سيؤول إليه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A report says Hagar belonged to Sarah, who gave her to Abraham; after Hagar bore Ishmael, Sarah became jealous and asked Abraham to remove them, so he settled them in Mecca.
rows.anchor: روي أن هاجر كانت لسارة رضي الله عنها فوهبتها لإبراهيم عليه السلام فولدت منه إسماعيل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: The report continues that God brought forth Zamzam; Jurhum saw birds, reasoned that birds gather only near water, found Hagar and the spring, asked to share water in exchange for milk, and she agreed.
rows.anchor: فأظهر الله عين زمزم، ثم إن جرهم رأوا ثم طيورا فقالوا لا طير إلا على الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām is purposive and attaches to “I settled”: Abraham settled them in that barren, isolated valley only so they would pray at the Sacred House.
rows.anchor: اللام لام كي وهي متعلقة بأسكنت أي ما أسكنتهم بهذا الوادي البلقع من كل مرتفق ومرتزق إلا لإقامة الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the address to God and placing it here signal that prayer is the central purpose of settling them there; Abraham seeks divine enabling for it.
rows.anchor: وتكرير النداء وتوسيطه للاشعار بأنها المقصودة بالذات من إسكانهم ثمة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative reads the lām as imperative: Abraham is asking God to enable his family to establish prayer, as if he had asked them to pray.
rows.anchor: وقيل لام الأمر والمراد هو الدعاء لهم بإقامة الصلاة كأنه طلب منهم الإقامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means hearts from among people’s hearts; min is partitive, or it means hearts of some people, with min marking origin.
rows.anchor: أي أفئدة من أفئدة الناس، ومن للتبعيض ولذلك قيل لو قال أفئدة الناس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: It is said that had Abraham asked for all people’s hearts, Persians and Romans would have crowded there and Jews and Christians would have made pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: ولذلك قيل لو قال أفئدة الناس لازدحمت عليهم فارس والروم ولحجت اليهود والنصارى

rows.speaker: هشام
rows.claim: Hisham has a reported variant, with some uncertainty in transmission, reading afʾīdata with an added yāʾ after the hamza.
rows.anchor: وقرأ هشام أفئيدة بخلف عنه بياء بعد الهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Āfidah may be a metathesized form of afʾidah, like āduru from adʾuru, or an active participle for groups hastening toward them; afidah may also drop the hamza for ease and derive from afada.
rows.anchor: وقرىء آفدة وهو يحتمل أن يكون مقلوب أفئدة كآدر في أدؤر وأن يكون اسم فاعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their hearts hasten toward the family in longing and affection.
rows.anchor: تهوى إليهم تسرع إليهم شوقا وودادا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading is passive, “made to incline toward them”; another derives from hawā yahwī, “to love,” with its construction using ilā because it incorporates the sense of yearning toward.
rows.anchor: وقرىء تهوى على البناء للمفعول من أهوى إليه غيره وتهوى من هوى يهوي إذا أحب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham asks for fruit for them despite their home in a valley with no vegetation, so they may be grateful; God answered by making it a secure sanctuary to which fruits of every kind are brought, with fruits of all seasons present in one day.
rows.anchor: وارزقهم من الثمرت مع سكناهم واديا لا نبات فيه لعلهم يشكرون تلك النعمة فأجاب الله عز وجل دعوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows what they conceal and reveal, their circumstances and interests better than they do, and is more merciful to them; prayer is still offered to display servitude and need of mercy and to hasten divine favor.
rows.anchor: إنك أعلم بأحوالنا ومصالحنا وأرحم بنا منا بأنفسنا، فلا حاجة لنا إلى الطلب لكنا ندعوك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative says the concealed matter is grief at separation, while the open matter is entreaty to God and reliance on Him.
rows.anchor: وقيل ما نخفي من وجد الفرقة وما نعلن من التضرع إليك والتوكل عليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating “Our Lord” intensifies supplication and resort to God.
rows.anchor: وتكرير النداء للمبالغة في التضرع واللجأ إلى الله تعالى

words: وَمَا يَخْفَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ مِن شَىْءٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nothing is hidden from God because His knowledge is intrinsic and relates equally to every object; min is exhaustive.
rows.anchor: لأنه العالم بعلم ذاتي يستوي نسبته إلى كل معلوم، ومن للاستغراق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being established in prayer means performing it properly and regularly.
rows.anchor: { رب اجعلني مقيم الصلوة } معدلا لها مواظبا عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “And some of my descendants” coordinates with the object “me”; it is partitive because God has informed Abraham, or past nations show him, that some descendants will be unbelievers.
rows.anchor: { ومن ذريتي } عطف على المنصوب في { اجعلني } ، والتبعيض لعلمه بإعلام الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Accept my prayer” can mean answer my supplication or accept my worship.
rows.anchor: { ربنا وتقبل دعاء } واستجب دعائي أو وتقبل عبادتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address to the Prophet steadies him: God sees the wrongdoers’ every act and will punish it; it can also address anyone who ignorantly imagines God heedless or mistakes His forbearance for neglect.
rows.anchor: خطاب لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، والمراد به تثبيته على ما هو عليه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation treats the warning as consolation for the oppressed and a threat to the oppressor.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنه تسلية للمظلوم وتهديد للظالم

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads the verb with nūn: “We delay them.”
rows.anchor: { إنما يؤخرهم } يؤخر عذابهم وعن أبي عمرو بالنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their eyes stare fixedly and cannot settle in their sockets because of the horror they see.
rows.anchor: { ليوم تشخص فيه الأبصر } أي تشخص فيه أبصارهم فلا تقر في أماكنها من هول ما ترى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muhtiʿīn means either hurrying toward the caller or facing him with eyes unblinking in awe and fear; the root conveys turning toward something.
rows.anchor: { مهطعين } أي مسرعين إلى الداعي، أو مقبلين بأبصارهم لا يطرفون هيبة وخوفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their heads are raised.
rows.anchor: { مقنعي رؤوسهم } رافعيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Either their eyes remain fixed without blinking, or their gaze cannot return so they cannot look at themselves.
rows.anchor: { لا يرتد إليهم طرفهم } بل تثبت عيونهم شاخصة لا تطرف، أو لا يرجع إليهم نظرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their hearts are empty of understanding from bewilderment, like those of a fool or coward with no judgment or strength; alternatively, they are empty of good or hollow of truth. Zuhayr’s line uses hawāʾ of an empty ostrich breast.
rows.anchor: قال زهير: من الظلمان جؤجؤه هواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to warn is addressed to Muhammad.
rows.anchor: { وأنذر الناس } يا محمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day of punishment is either the Resurrection or the day of death, the first day of their punishment; grammatically, it is the second object of “warn.”
rows.anchor: { يوم يأتيهم العذاب } يعني يوم القيامة، أو يوم الموت فإنه أول أيام عذابهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers are those who committed idolatry and denial.
rows.anchor: { فيقول الذين ظلموا } بالشرك والتكذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask either for punishment to be postponed, for return to earthly life until a near term, or for their lives to be extended long enough to believe and answer the call.
rows.anchor: أخر العذاب عنا أو ردنا إلى الدنيا وأمهلنا إلى حد من الزمان قريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “We will answer Your call and follow the messengers” is the response to the imperative; 63:10 has a parallel construction.
rows.anchor: { نجب دعوتك ونتبع الرسل } جواب للأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording implies “you swore”; “you have no departure” answers their oath in matching direct address. They had claimed they would remain in this world and not die, perhaps from arrogance and false confidence, as their massive building and distant hopes suggest.
rows.anchor: { أولم تكونوا أقسمتم من قبل ما لكم من زوال } على إرادة القول و { ما لكم } جواب القسم جاء بلفظ الخطاب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says they swore there was no move to another abode and that after death they would remain in the same state until a later state.
rows.anchor: وقيل أقسموا أنهم لا ينتقلون إلى دار أخرى وأنهم إذا ماتوا لا يزالون على تلك الحالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “and they do not delay,” the pronoun is masculine because ummah is treated according to its meaning.
rows.anchor: وتذكير ضمير { أمة } فيه للحمل على المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists address the Prophet with this title mockingly, then call him mad for claiming that God sent down the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: نادوا به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم على التهكم، ألا ترى إلى ما نادوه له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their taunt means that claiming God sent down the Qur’an sounds mad, as Pharaoh similarly called his messenger mad in 26:27.
rows.anchor: ونظير ذلك قول فرعون: إن رسولكم الذى أرسل إليكم لمجنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Law is combined with mā as it is with lā, expressing either impossibility due to another circumstance or an exhortation.
rows.anchor: ركب { لو } مع { ما } كما ركبت مع لا لمعنيين امتناع الشيء لوجود غيره والتحضيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They demand angels either to affirm and support the prophetic mission, as in 25:7, or to bring punishment for their denial as happened to earlier peoples.
rows.anchor: ليصدقوك ويعضدوك على الدعوة كقوله تعالى: لولا أنزل إليه ملك فيكون معه نذيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condition challenges the Prophet’s claim to be truthful.
rows.anchor: { إن كنت من الصدقين } في دعواك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading has yāʾ and accusative “the angels,” with God as subject; Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Ḥafṣ read nūn, while Abū Bakr has tāʾ and passive voice with “angels” nominative; another reading means “descend repeatedly.”
rows.anchor: { ما ينزل الملئكة } بالياء ونصب { الملئكة } على أن الضمير لله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels descend only in accordance with truth, the occasion set by divine wisdom; appearing visibly would add confusion, and hastening punishment would harm those among the people and their descendants destined to believe.
rows.anchor: { إلا بالحق } إلا تنزيلا ملتبسا بالحق أي بالوجه الذي قدره واقتضته حكمته

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative takes “truth” to mean revelation or punishment.
rows.anchor: وقيل الحق الوحي أو العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idhan answers the demand: if angels were sent, the people would not be granted any delay; the conditional premise is understood.
rows.anchor: { إذا } جواب لهم وجزاء لشرط مقدر أي ولو نزلنا الملائكة ما كانوا منظرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration answers their denial and mockery and is reinforced by several emphatic forms.
rows.anchor: رد لإنكارهم واستهزائهم ولذلك أكده من وجوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God preserves the Qur’an from distortion, additions, and omissions by making its miraculous composition impossible to alter without language experts noticing, or by guaranteeing that no flaw enters it over time.
rows.anchor: أي من التحريف والزيادة والنقص بأن جعلناه معجزا مباينا لكلام البشر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative takes the pronoun in “for it” to refer to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وقيل الضمير في { له } للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening means: remember the time when your Lord said to the angels that He would create a human from sounding clay and altered dark mud.
rows.anchor: { وإذ قال ربك } واذكر وقت قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When God has proportioned the human, He has balanced and prepared his form for the spirit to be breathed into him.
rows.anchor: عدلت خلقته وهيأته لنفخ الروح فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spirit’s effects flow through bodily cavities and bring the human to life; “breathing” is a metaphor for its attachment to the body, since spirit first attaches to subtle vapor from the heart and spreads through the arteries.
rows.anchor: حتى جرى آثاره في تجاويف أعضائه فحيي، وأصل النفخ إجراء الريح في تجويف جسم آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spirit is attributed to God Himself for the reason explained earlier in the commentary on Sūrat al-Nisāʾ.
rows.anchor: وإضافة الروح إلى نفسه لما مر في «النساء»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa-qaʿū means “fall down”; sājidīn is an imperative from waqaʿa, “to fall.”
rows.anchor: { فقعوا له } فاسقطوا له. { سجدين } أمر من وقع يقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After many proofs of God’s power, wisdom, and sole creation of the things enumerated, the rhetorical question rejects equating Him with beings unable to create anything.
rows.anchor: { أفمن يخلق كمن لا يخلق } إنكار بعد إقامة الدلائل المتكاثرة على كمال قدرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording reverses the expected order (“Can one who does not create equal one who creates?”) to expose how associators have put God among powerless created beings.
rows.anchor: وكان حق الكلام أفمن لا يخلق كمن يخلق، لكنه عكس تنبيها على أنهم بالإشراك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The non-creators are everything worshipped besides God, either including rational beings among them or referring to idols; idols are treated as rational because they are called gods, for rhetorical symmetry, or for emphasis.
rows.anchor: والمراد بمن لا يخلق كل ما عبد من دون الله سبحانه وتعالى مغلبا فيه أولو العلم منهم أو الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols are grammatically treated like rational beings because worshippers call them gods and a deity should know, to match the creator/non-creator contrast, or for emphatic force.
rows.anchor: وأجروها مجرى أولي العلم لأنهم سموها آلهة ومن حق الإله أن يعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They should recognize the error, which is so obvious that reason reaches it by merely recalling and attending to it.
rows.anchor: فإنه لجلائه كالحاصل للعقل الذي يحضر عنده بأدنى تذكر والتفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those invoked besides God are the gods that the hearers worship besides Him.
rows.anchor: { والذين يدعون من دون الله } أي والآلهة الذين تعبدونهم من دونه

rows.speaker: أبو بكر وحفص
rows.claim: Abū Bakr reads yadʿūna with yāʾ; Ḥafṣ reads all three occurrences in the nearby passage with yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو بكر «يدعون» بالياء. وقرأ حفص ثلاثتها بالياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their inability to create anything establishes that they do not share God’s creative power, already shown to distinguish creator from non-creator.
rows.anchor: لما نفى المشاركة بين من يخلق ومن لا يخلق بين أنهم لا يخلقون شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are contingent beings whose existence depends on being created, while a deity must exist necessarily.
rows.anchor: لأنهم ذوات ممكنة مفتقرة الوجود إلى التخليق، والإله ينبغي أن يكون واجب الوجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What people possess refers to the transient things of this world, which run out and perish.
rows.anchor: { ما عندكم } من أعراض الدنيا. { ينفد } ينقضي ويفنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What is with God refers to the stores of His mercy, which do not run out.
rows.anchor: { وما عند الله } من خزائن رحمته. { باق } لا ينفد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause explains the preceding ruling and proves that the bliss of Paradise’s inhabitants is everlasting.
rows.anchor: وهو تعليل للحكم السابق ودليل على أن نعيم أهل الجنة باق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The patient are those who endured poverty and unbelievers’ abuse, or the burdens of religious obligations.
rows.anchor: على الفاقة وأذى الكفار، أو على مشاق التكاليف

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وعاصم
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr and ʿĀṣim read the verb with nūn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وعاصم بالنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The recompense is either according to the best-weighted deeds, such as obligatory and recommended acts, or a reward better than their deeds.
rows.anchor: بما يرجح فعله من أعمالهم كالواجبات والمندوبات، أو بجزاء أحسن من أعمالهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause can predicate the opening “Ṭā Hā” if it is a subject understood as the sūra, or relate the Qur’an as an antecedent; depending on how Ṭā Hā is read, it can also be a response to an oath, a response to a vocative, or an independent sentence with an omitted subject or quoted letters.
rows.anchor: إن جعلته مبتدأ على أنه مؤول بالسورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet was not sent the Qur’an to suffer from excessive grief over Quraysh’s unbelief, since his duty is only to convey it, or from extreme ascetic discipline and prolonged night prayer.
rows.anchor: ما عليك إلا أن تبلغ، أو بكثرة الرياضة وكثرة التهجد والقيام على ساق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shaqā is commonly used to mean fatigue, as in the sayings “the horse trainer suffers most” and “the chief of the people is their most burdened.”
rows.anchor: والشقاء شائع بمعنى التعب ومنه أشقى من رائض المهر، وسيد القوم أشقاهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The choice of “suffer” hints that the Qur’an was sent to make the Prophet blessed and happy.
rows.anchor: ولعله عدل إليه للإشعار بأنه أنزل عليه ليسعد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative says this refutes disbelievers who saw the Prophet’s worship and claimed he suffered by leaving their religion and that the Qur’an was sent to make him suffer.
rows.anchor: وقيل رد وتكذيب للكفرة، فإنهم لما رأوا كثرة عبادته قالوا إنك لتشقى بترك ديننا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Illā tadhkiratan means “rather, as a reminder” and is an exception disconnected from the preceding phrase.
rows.anchor: { إلا تذكرة } لكن تذكيرا، وانتصابها على الاستثناء المنقطع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It cannot substitute for the grammatical position of “so that you suffer,” because the two are different kinds, or be a second purpose of “We sent down,” since one act does not take two causes.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يكون بدلا من محل { لتشقى } لاختلاف الجنسين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other analyses make the verbal noun circumstantial of the Prophet or Qur’an, or a purpose attached to an omitted description of the Qur’an (“the Qur’an sent to make you suffer”).
rows.anchor: وقيل هو مصدر في موقع الحال من الكاف أو القرآن، أو مفعول له على أن { لتشقى } متعلق بمحذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who fear are either receptive people with tender hearts affected by warning or those God knows will fear through warning and benefit from it.
rows.anchor: لمن في قلبه خشية ورقة تتأثر بالإنذار، أو لمن علم الله منه أنه يخشى بالتخويف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if one speaks aloud in remembrance or prayer, God needs no loudness because He knows the secret and what is still more hidden: the thought within the self.
rows.anchor: وإن تجهر بذكر الله ودعائه فاعلم أنه غني عن جهرك فإنه سبحانه يعلم السر وأخفى منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembrance and loud supplication are prescribed not to inform God, but to form and root remembrance in the self, keep it from distraction, and humble it through earnest prayer.
rows.anchor: ليس لإعلام الله بل لتصوير النفس بالذكر ورسوخه فيها ومنعها عن الاشتغال بغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Having established that God possesses the attributes of divinity, the discussion proceeds to affirm that He alone possesses them and their implications.
rows.anchor: لما ظهر بذلك أنه المستجمع لصفات الألوهية بين أنه المتفرد بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question draws Moses’ attention to the marvels God is about to show through the object.
rows.anchor: { وما تلك } استفهام يتضمن استيقاظا لما يريه فيها من العجائب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “In your right hand” is either circumstantial to the sense of the demonstrative or attached to “that.”
rows.anchor: { بيمينك } حال من معنى الإشارة، وقيل صلة { تلك }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the vocative “Moses” adds intimacy and draws his attention.
rows.anchor: { يا موسى } تكرير لزيادة الاستئناس والتنبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has ʿuṣiyy, following the dialect of Hudhayl.
rows.anchor: { قال هي عصاي } وقرىء «عصي» على لغة هذيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses leans on the staff when tired or when standing at the head of his flock.
rows.anchor: { أتوكؤا عليها } أعتمد عليها إذا أعييت أو وقفت على رأس القطيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hashsh means shaking leaves down onto his sheep; the verb is compared to brittle bread breaking apart.
rows.anchor: { وأهش بها على غنمي } وأخبط الورق بها على رؤوس غنمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading repeats ahushsh; another has sīn, from hass, to drive or urge sheep, meaning he signals to them as he drives them.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { أهش } وكلاهما من هش الخبز يهش إذا انكسر لهشاشته، وقرىء بالسين من الهس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His other uses include carrying tools from its fork, hanging a cloth for shade, extending a short rope, and fighting predators that approach the flock.
rows.anchor: مثل أن كان إذا سار ألقاها على عاتقه فعلق بها أدواته، وعرض الزندين على شعبيتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses understood the question to invite an account of the staff’s identity and uses, preparing a contrast with its later supernatural qualities, which God created as signs rather than natural properties.
rows.anchor: وكأنه صلى الله عليه وسلم فهم أن المقصود من السؤال أن يذكر حقيقتها وما يرى من منافعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its later signs include glowing forks, becoming a bucket, lengthening to a well’s depth, defending Moses, producing or draining water, and bearing the fruit he wanted.
rows.anchor: مثل أن تشتعل شعبتاه بالليل كالشمع، وتصيران دلوا عند الاستقاء، وتطول بطول البئر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses feared and fled when the staff became a swiftly moving serpent that swallowed stones and trees.
rows.anchor: فإنه لما رآها حية تسرع وتبتلع الحجر والشجر خاف وهرب منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sīratahā al-ūlā means its former form or condition; the noun derives from “to proceed” and is figuratively used for a way or state.
rows.anchor: هيئتها وحالتها المتقدمة، وهي فعلة من السير تجوز بها للطريقة والهيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may be accusative with a deleted preposition, from causative aʿāda derived from ʿāda, or adverbial (“in its former way”); it may also imply that the staff will again move as before and serve Moses.
rows.anchor: وانتصابها على نزع الخافض أو على أن أعاد منقول من عاده بمعنى عاد إليه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: It is said that God’s reassurance calmed Moses so fully that he put his hand into the serpent’s mouth and took it by the jaws.
rows.anchor: قيل لما قال له ربه ذلك اطمأنت نفسه حتى أدخل يده في فمها وأخذ بلحييها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faced with a grave mission, Moses asks for an expanded heart to carry its burdens, endure its hardships, and receive revelation, and asks God to ease the task by creating means and removing obstacles.
rows.anchor: لما أمره الله بخطب عظيم وأمر جسيم سأله أن يشرح صدره ويفسح قلبه لتحمل أعبائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The initial “for me” leaves the requested expansion and facilitation general before “my breast” and “my task” specify them, adding emphasis.
rows.anchor: وفائدة لي إبهام المشروح والميسر أولا، ثم رفعه بذكر الصدر والأمر تأكيدا ومبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Clear delivery is needed for effective proclamation; Moses had a speech impediment from putting an ember in his mouth.
rows.anchor: فإنما يحسن التبليغ من البليغ وكان في لسانه رتة من جمرة أدخلها فاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Pharaoh carried Moses as a child; Moses seized and pulled Pharaoh’s beard, so Pharaoh ordered his death, but Asiya said he could not distinguish an ember from a ruby. Offered both, Moses put the ember in his mouth; perhaps this explains his whitened hand.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن فرعون حمله يوما فأخذ بلحيته ونتفها، فغضب وأمر بقتله فقالت آسية

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account says Moses burned his hand, Pharaoh unsuccessfully tried to heal it, and Moses later said he called Pharaoh to the one who healed what Pharaoh could not.
rows.anchor: وقيل احترقت يده فاجتهد فرعون في علاجها فلم تبرأ، ثم لما دعاه قال إلى أي رب تدعوني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Commentators disagree whether Moses’ speech impediment was completely removed: those affirming full recovery cite 20:36, “You have been granted your request.”
rows.anchor: واختلف في زوال العقدة بكمالها فمن قال به تمسك بقوله قد أوتيت سؤلك يموسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those denying complete recovery cite Moses’ claim that Aaron is more eloquent in 28:34 and the accusation that he can scarcely speak in 43:52.
rows.anchor: ومن لم يقل احتج بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The grant of Moses’ request does not prove total recovery: he asked only to remove an impediment to being understood, as the indefinite “a knot” and the purpose “so they understand” show.
rows.anchor: وأجاب عن الأول بأنه لم يسأل حل عقدة لسانه مطلقا بل عقدة تمنع الإفهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min lisānī may describe the knot or be attached directly to the verb “untie.”
rows.anchor: ومن لساني يحتمل أن يكون صفة عقدة وأن يكون صلة احلل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “With My signs” means with My miracles.
rows.anchor: { اذهب أنت وأخوك بئايتى } بمعجزاتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means do not slacken or fall short.
rows.anchor: { ولا تنيا } ولا تفترا ولا تقصرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has kasra on the tāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { تنيا } بكسر التاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “In My remembrance” means do not forget God wherever they go, or do not slacken in proclaiming His remembrance and calling people to it.
rows.anchor: وقيل في تبليغ ذكري والدعاء إلي
